The [[Tamil language]] has [[Numeral (linguistics)|number words]] and dedicated symbols for them in the [[Tamil script]]. They have mostly been supplanted by [[Arabic numeral]]s in common usage.

==Basic numbering in Tamil (Tamil Illakkam)==

===Zero===

Old Tamil possesses a special numerical character for zero ''(see [[#Old Tamil numerals|Old Tamil numerals]] below),'' which is read as {{translit|ta|ISO|andru}} (literally, no/nothing). Modern Tamil words for zero include {{lang|ta|சுழியம்}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|suḻiyam}}) or {{lang|ta|பூஜ்ஜியம்}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|pūjjiyam}}).

==Transcribing other numbers==

===Reproductive and attributive prefixes===
Tamil has a numeric prefix for each number from 1 to 9, which can be added to the words for the powers of ten (ten, hundred, thousand, etc.) to form multiples of them. For instance, the word for fifty, {{lang|ta|ஐம்பது}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|aimpatu}}) is a combination of {{lang|ta|ஐ}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|ai}}, the prefix for five) and {{lang|ta|பத்து}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|pattu}}, which is ten). The prefix for nine changes with respect to the succeeding base 10. {{lang|ta|தொ}} + the unvoiced consonant of the succeeding base 10 forms the prefix for nine. For instance, 90 is {{lang|ta|தொ}} + {{lang|ta|ண்}} ({{lang|ta|ண்}} being the unvoiced version of {{lang|ta|ணூ}}), hence, {{lang|ta|தொண்ணூறு}}).

These are typically void in the Tamil language except for some Hindu references; for example, {{lang|ta|அட்ட இலட்சுமிகள்}} (the eight Lakshmis). Even in religious contexts, the Tamil language is usually more preferred for its more poetic nature and relatively low incidence of consonant clusters.

===Specific characters===
Unlike other modern Indian number systems, Tamil has distinct digits for 10, 100, and 1000. It also has distinct characters for other number-based aspects of day-to-day life.

===Partitive numerals ({{lang|ta|பகுத்தல்}})===

====Fractions ({{lang|ta|பின்னம்}})====
Proposals to encode Tamil [[Fraction (mathematics)|fractions]] and symbols to [[Unicode]] were submitted.<ref>Sharma, Shriramana. (2012). ''Proposal to encode Tamil fractions and symbols''. Retrieved 12 March 2019 from https://www.unicode.org/L2/L2012/12231-tamil-fractions-symbols-proposal.pdf</ref><ref>Government of Tamil Nadu. (2017). ''Finalized proposal to encode Tamil fractions and symbols''. Retrieved 12 March 2019 from http://unicode.org/wg2/docs/n4822-tamil-frac.pdf</ref> As of version 12.0, [[Tamil Supplement|Tamil characters]] used for fractional values in traditional accounting practices were added to the Unicode Standard.

=====Transcribing fractions ({{lang|ta|பின்னம் எழுத்தல்}})=====
Any fraction can be transcribed by affixing -{{lang|ta|இல்}} (-il) after the [[denominator]] followed by the [[numerator]]. For instance, 1/41 can be said as {{lang|ta|நாற்பத்து ஒன்றில் ஒன்று}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|nāṟpattu oṉṟil oṉṟu}}).

The suffixing of the -{{lang|ta|இல்}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|-il}}) requires the last consonant of the number to be changed to its {{lang|ta|இ}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|i}}) form. For example, {{lang|ta|மூன்று}} + {{lang|ta|இல்}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|mūṉṟu}} + {{translit|ta|ISO|-il}}) becomes {{lang|ta|மூன்றில்}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|mūṉṟil}}); note the {{lang|ta|உ}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|u}}) has been omitted.

'''Common fractions ({{lang|ta|பொது பின்னங்கள்}})''' have names already allocated to them, hence, these names are often used rather than the above method.

{{note|a}} ''Aṇu'' was considered as the lowest fraction by ancient Tamils as size of smallest physical object (similar to an atom). Later, this term went to Sanskrit to refer directly to atoms.{{Citation needed|date=January 2023|reason=Doubtful}}

====Decimals ({{lang|ta|பதின்மம்}})====
Decimal point is called {{lang|ta|புள்ளி}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|puḷḷi}}) in [[Tamil language|Tamil]]. For example, 1.1 would be read as {{lang|ta|ஒன்று புள்ளி ஒன்று}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|oṉṟu puḷḷi oṉṟu}}). In Sri Lankan Tamil, Thasam தசம்.

====Percentage ({{lang|ta|விழுக்காடு}})====
Percentage is known as {{lang|ta|விழுக்காடு}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|viḻukkāḍu}}) in [[Tamil language|Tamil]] or {{lang|ta|சதவீதம்}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|śatavītam}}). These words are simply added after a number to form percentages. For instance, four percent is {{lang|ta|நான்கு சதவீதம்}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|nāṉku satavītam}}) or {{lang|ta|நான்கு விழுக்காடு}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|nāṉku viḻukkāḍu}}). Percentage symbol (%) is also recognised and used.

===Ordinal numbers ({{lang|ta|வரிசை எண்கள்}})===
Ordinal numbers are formed by adding the suffix -{{lang|ta|ஆம்}} ({{translit|ta|ISO|ām}}) after the number, except for 'First'.

Also, [[Tamil language|Tamil]] through the [[Pallava script]] which itself through the [[Kawi script]], [[Khmer script]] and other South-east Asian scripts has shaped the numeral [[grapheme]] of most South-east Asian languages.

==History==
Before the [[Government of India]] unveiled {{Indian rupee}} as the new [[Indian rupee sign|rupee symbol]], people in Tamil Nadu used the Tamil letter {{lang|ta|௹}} as the symbol. This symbol continues to be used occasionally as rupee symbol by Indian Tamils. It is also used by Tamils in Sri Lanka.<ref>{{Cite web |last=B |first=Sara |date=2022-05-05 |title=Travel Insurance for Sri Lanka |url=https://www.insuremytrip.com/destinations/sri-lanka-travel-insurance/ |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=InsureMyTrip |language=en-US}}</ref>

The symbol {{lang|ta|௳}} is also known as the {{translit|ta|ISO|Piḷḷaiyār Suḻi}} ({{lit|Curl of {{translit|ta|ISO|Piḷḷaiyār}}}}), a symbol that most [[Tamil people|Tamil]] Hindus will start off any auspicious document with. It is written to invoke the god {{translit|ta|ISO|Piḷḷaiyār}}, known otherwise as [[Ganesha]], who is the remover of obstacles.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Pattanaik |first=Devdutt |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Wh22qvzQuowC&dq=pillaiyar+suzhi&pg=RA1-PA62-IA3 |title=99 Thoughts on Ganesha |date=2015-01-27 |publisher=Jaico Publishing House |isbn=978-81-8495-152-3 |language=en}}</ref>
